track.name: psychology
track.label: Behavioral Psychology
track.summary: Learn how people actually decide and behave — heuristics, biases, motivation, and habit formation — so you can design products, marketing, and policies that work with human nature instead of against it.

phases.title: Foundations of Judgment & Decision-Making
phases.description: How the mind actually makes decisions — the two systems of thinking and the mental shortcuts behind everyday judgment.

phases.title: Cognitive Biases in Practice
phases.description: The specific biases — anchoring, loss aversion, social proof, scarcity — that predictably distort how people judge value and take action.

phases.title: Behavior Change Models
phases.description: Frameworks for designing behavior itself: what has to be true for an action to happen, and how habits form and stick.

phases.title: Motivation & Engagement
phases.description: What actually drives people to keep engaging — the difference between internal and external motivators, and how gamification and flow keep people coming back.

phases.title: Applying Behavioral Psychology to Product & Marketing
phases.description: Turning the theory into practice — nudges, choice architecture, and where persuasive design crosses the line into manipulation.

phases.title: Behavioral Economics Fundamentals
phases.description: The economic side of the same ideas — how people actually value gains, losses, and money — plus a full free course to go deeper.

topics.title: System 1 vs. System 2 Thinking
topics.description: How the brain's fast, automatic thinking and its slow, deliberate thinking trade off in everyday decisions.

topics.title: Heuristics: Mental Shortcuts in Decision-Making
topics.description: The rules of thumb people use to decide quickly, and why they help more often than they hurt.

topics.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow — Kahneman's Framework
topics.description: The book and researcher that turned System 1/2 thinking and dozens of biases into a shared vocabulary for the field.

topics.title: Anchoring & Framing Effects
topics.description: How the first number you see and the way a choice is worded quietly shape the decision that follows.

topics.title: Loss Aversion & the Endowment Effect
topics.description: Why losing something feels worse than gaining the equivalent, and why owning something makes us overvalue it.

topics.title: Social Proof & Scarcity
topics.description: Why we copy what others are doing and want more of what seems limited or about to disappear.

topics.title: The Fogg Behavior Model
topics.description: BJ Fogg's model of exactly what has to line up — motivation, ability, and a prompt — for a behavior to happen.

topics.title: Habit Loops: Cue, Routine, Reward
topics.description: How a repeated cue-routine-reward cycle turns a deliberate action into an automatic habit.

topics.title: The Hook Model: Building Habit-Forming Products
topics.description: Nir Eyal's trigger-action-variable reward-investment loop for designing products people return to on their own.

topics.title: Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Motivation
topics.description: The difference between doing something because it's rewarding in itself and doing it for an outside reward or to avoid a penalty.

topics.title: Gamification & the Octalysis Framework
topics.description: Yu-kai Chou's map of the eight core human drives that game-like design elements tap into.

topics.title: Flow, Feedback Loops & Engagement Design
topics.description: Csikszentmihalyi's flow state, and why fast, clear feedback is what keeps people absorbed in a task or product.

topics.title: Nudge Theory & Choice Architecture
topics.description: How the way options are presented — the default, the order, the framing — steers decisions without removing any choice.

topics.title: Dark Patterns & the Ethics of Persuasion
topics.description: Where nudging crosses into deception, and the manipulative UX patterns regulators are now cracking down on.

topics.title: Behavioral Design in Marketing & UX
topics.description: Applying behavioral science deliberately inside product and marketing design, rather than bolting psychology on after the fact.

topics.title: Prospect Theory
topics.description: Kahneman and Tversky's model of how people actually weigh risky gains and losses, and why it beats the classical rational-agent model.

topics.title: Mental Accounting
topics.description: Why people mentally sort money into separate 'accounts' and treat a dollar differently depending on where it came from.

topics.title: Intro to Behavioral Economics
topics.description: A field-level overview of behavioral economics, plus a full free course for going deeper than any single article can.

resources.title: System 1 and System 2 Thinking
resources.note: Clear reference-guide explanation of Kahneman's two-system model and why it matters for decision-making.

resources.title: System 1 vs. System 2 - Highlights from Thinking Fast and Slow
resources.note: A short visual walkthrough of the two systems for anyone who'd rather watch than read.

resources.title: Heuristics: Definition, Examples, And How They Work
resources.note: Grounds the term 'heuristic' with its history and clear everyday examples.

resources.title: Heuristics
resources.note: Connects heuristics directly to the biases covered later in this track.

resources.title: Thinking Fast and Slow Summary
resources.note: A fast, free run-through of Kahneman's core argument before diving into individual biases.

resources.title: Thinking Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman: Animated Summary with focus on 'System 1 & 2'
resources.note: An animated recap that keeps the two-systems idea visual and memorable.

resources.title: Anchoring Bias
resources.note: Explains why the first number on the table skews every estimate that follows, with a pricing example.

resources.title: Framing Effect In Psychology
resources.note: Shows how identical information framed as a gain vs. a loss changes what people choose.

resources.title: Loss Aversion
resources.note: The Kahneman/Tversky finding that losses hurt roughly twice as much as equivalent gains feel good.

resources.title: Endowment Effect
resources.note: Why simply owning something makes people demand more to give it up than they'd pay to acquire it.

resources.title: Social Proof
resources.note: Uses a 61-million-person Facebook experiment to show how visible peer behavior changes our own.

resources.title: Scarcity
resources.note: Explains why limited availability alone makes something feel more valuable and urgent.

resources.title: Fogg Behavior Model
resources.note: The model's own home page, straight from BJ Fogg's Stanford Behavior Design Lab.

resources.title: Learn the Fogg Behavior Model
resources.note: A guided, self-paced walkthrough of motivation, ability, and prompts with worked examples.

resources.title: CAR Model
resources.note: Breaks the cue-action-reward habit loop into its three parts with practical framing.

resources.title: The Habit Loop: 5 Habit Triggers That Make New Behaviors Stick
resources.note: A practical look at the cue side of the loop — the five types of triggers that actually start a habit.

resources.title: Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products
resources.note: Nir Eyal's own page introducing the book and the Hook Model it's built around.

resources.title: Nir Eyal's Hooked Model: Trigger, Action, Variable Reward, Investment
resources.note: A clean, standalone walkthrough of all four Hook Model steps for anyone who wants the model without reading the book.

resources.title: Extrinsic vs. Intrinsic Motivation: What's the Difference?
resources.note: Lays out both motivation types side by side with research on where each works best.

resources.title: The Puzzle of Motivation
resources.note: Dan Pink's widely-viewed talk on why extrinsic rewards can backfire on complex, creative work.

resources.title: Learn Gamification: The Octalysis Framework (8 Core Drives)
resources.note: The framework's own explainer of all eight core drives, straight from its creator's site.

resources.title: Gamification to Improve Our World: Yu-kai Chou at TEDxLausanne
resources.note: Chou's own talk on why well-designed gamification is more than points and badges.

resources.title: Mihály Csíkszentmihályi: The Father of Flow
resources.note: Covers the researcher, the theory, and the conditions that produce a flow state.

resources.title: Flow, the Secret to Happiness
resources.note: Csikszentmihalyi explaining flow in his own words — useful for connecting the theory back to real engagement.

resources.title: Nudge Theory
resources.note: Traces nudge theory back to Thaler and Sunstein and to what counts as a nudge versus a mandate.

resources.title: Choice Architecture
resources.note: Explains how the design of a decision environment shapes the choice itself, for better or worse.

resources.title: The Dark (Patterns) Side of UX Design
resources.note: From the site that coined 'dark patterns' — a grounded look at where persuasive UX turns manipulative.

resources.title: Dark Patterns: Brignull's 12 Manipulative UX Tricks
resources.note: Walks through Brignull's original 12-pattern taxonomy with concrete examples of each.

resources.title: Behavioral Science to Elevate User Experience (UX) Design
resources.note: Makes the direct case for using behavioral science principles deliberately in UX design decisions.

resources.title: Stop Designing for the Average User
resources.note: A behavioral-science argument against one-size-fits-all design, with implications for marketing segmentation too.

resources.title: Prospect Theory
resources.note: Explains the reference points and asymmetric weighting of gains and losses at the core of the theory.

resources.title: Prospect Theory in Psychology: Loss Aversion Bias
resources.note: A second pass at prospect theory with more of the underlying experiments Kahneman and Tversky ran.

resources.title: Mental Accounting
resources.note: Richard Thaler's concept of separate mental 'budgets,' with the classic movie-ticket example.

resources.title: This Is Your Brain On Money
resources.note: Applies mental accounting and related biases to everyday spending decisions.

resources.title: Behavioral Economics
resources.note: A field-level overview tying together everything the earlier phases covered piece by piece.

resources.title: Behavioural Economics in Action
resources.note: A free-to-audit multi-week course for going deeper than any single article, taught by Rotman's Dilip Soman.
